name: Factor Timing
rationale: Factor timing rules test whether value, quality, momentum, or low-volatility factor exposure should change by regime.
expected_benefit: Potentially better diversification and risk-adjusted return than broad market timing.
failure_modes: Factor definitions may be unavailable or inconsistent.
Signals can be slow and regime-dependent.

canonical_variants.name: Value/momentum rotation
canonical_variants.description: Rotate between value and momentum factor ETFs using relative strength.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: Rotating between value and momentum factor ETFs may improve Sharpe versus a static factor blend.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe after turnover costs and avoid worse max drawdown.

canonical_variants.name: Low-volatility factor defensive switch
canonical_variants.description: Move toward low-volatility factor exposure during stressed regimes.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A low-volatility factor switch may reduce equity drawdown while preserving more return than cash.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 75% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Quality plus momentum confirmation
canonical_variants.description: Hold equity factor exposure only when quality and momentum proxies agree.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: Requiring quality and momentum confirmation may reduce weak-factor periods without excessive turnover.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe versus a static blend after realistic costs.

suggested_validation: Start with ETF proxies before security-level factor data.
Use a static factor blend benchmark.
Avoid broad lookback sweeps until one hypothesis survives.
execution_notes: The current engine lacks cross-sectional factor ranking and scheduled factor rotation.
